teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: The source speech/video is controlled by the teacher. The bank is an unapproved audio-dependent draft; original clip and facts require independent linguistic verification before use.

objective.q: Why does Ford's comment about receiving the award 'a little early' matter beyond being a joke?
options: He wishes another performer had received the honour first.
He sees the recognition as part of an unfinished career.
He intends to stop working immediately after the ceremony.
He believes awards cannot reflect the quality of acting.
objective.explanation: The humour points to his continuing professional life rather than a completed career.
objective.sourceEvidence: Still a working actor; jokes that the lifetime achievement award is early.

objective.q: Which contrast best captures the way he describes his early professional life?
options: He immediately found the right role but later became dissatisfied.
He always valued technical work more than performing.
He trained actors while waiting to become a director.
His route into acting involved uncertainty and work outside acting.
objective.explanation: The speech refers to a long struggle before his breakthrough and carpentry between acting jobs.
objective.sourceEvidence: A struggle of about fifteen years; moved between acting work and carpentry.

objective.q: What is the deeper function of recalling the people involved in plays at college?
options: It shows how finding a community gave his ambitions direction.
It proves that his classmates were all future film stars.
It suggests that formal teaching was irrelevant to his career.
It explains why he would have preferred working only on stage.
objective.explanation: The theatre group gave him a sense of purpose and belonging during a difficult period.
objective.sourceEvidence: At college he found people putting on plays and a place to belong.

objective.q: Why does the speaker repeatedly acknowledge people behind the camera?
options: To explain why awards should only go to technical staff.
To show that different film jobs can be done by one person.
To challenge the idea that success belongs to the visible star alone.
To suggest that acting matters less than writing or directing.
objective.explanation: His thanks frame filmmaking as collective effort involving cast, writers, directors and crew.
objective.sourceEvidence: Recognises writers, directors, cast and every crew member.

objective.q: A successful performer wants to follow the principle Ford expresses near the end. What should they do?
options: Limit opportunities for younger colleagues to protect their own career.
Use their position to support others and widen access to opportunities.
Avoid taking responsibility outside their own performance.
Focus on personal recognition as evidence of professional quality.
objective.explanation: Ford associates success and freedom with responsibility towards other people.
objective.sourceEvidence: Success creates freedom but also responsibility towards others.

objective.q: Which statement best applies Ford's remarks about stories to a school theatre project?
options: The best result is always the performance with the largest audience.
The personal experience of a performer matters more than that of viewers.
A compelling story matters only if it presents an accurate biography.
A performance can make viewers feel connected through shared experiences.
objective.explanation: Ford describes storytelling as a means of emotional connection and shared experience.
objective.sourceEvidence: Stories can create emotional connection and bring people together.

written.q: Explain how Ford balances humour with gratitude in his speech. Give one specific example of each.
written.modelAnswer: His joke that the honour comes a little early makes the speech light, while his thanks to collaborators and supporters express sincere gratitude.
written.teacherCriterion: 1 point only if the response includes a specific instance of humour AND a supported expression of gratitude, explaining their effect.
written.sourceEvidence: Early joke about the award; repeated recognition of others.

written.q: In your own words, explain how Ford links belonging to his development as an actor. Refer to one moment he describes.
written.modelAnswer: Finding the people putting on plays at college gave him a sense of belonging and helped him see acting as a direction he could pursue.
written.teacherCriterion: 1 point for a clear link between community/belonging and the development of his ambitions, supported by the college theatre example.
written.sourceEvidence: College theatre group provided a place to belong and a sense of direction.
